title: Peak-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.23328v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Real-time inference on small devices needs low activation memory without extra latency, which makes operator order the most valuable memory lever: it is free in time. We show that the usual way of deploying a better order, handing it back to the compiler and regenerating code, is unreliable. In PyTorch Inductor the regenerated program misses its predicted peak in 22 of 54 CPU configurations. It is worse than the stock program in 9 of them and in 19 of 50 on a GPU, and on the GPU it also changes numerical results. We instead profile the generated program, model its memory exactly from its own statements and their read/write effects, and permute those statements. We prove that this realizes the modeled peak whenever allocation does not depend on history. It does so to the byte, with bitwise-identical results, in all our CPU runs. On the GPU we characterize why the caching allocator breaks the condition. To know when to stop, we give forwar

translated_title: 可信的峰值内存调度：精确实现、可认证的最优性，以及推理中重计算的极限
translated_abstract: 在小型设备上进行实时推理需要在无额外延迟的前提下实现低激活内存，这使算子顺序成为最有价值的内存调控手段：它在时间上是零成本的。我们证明了通常部署更优顺序的做法——将其交还给编译器并重新生成代码——是不可靠的。在PyTorch Inductor中，重新生成的程序在54个CPU配置中有22个未能达到预测的内存峰值，其中9个比原始程序更差；在GPU的50个配置中有19个如此，并且在GPU上它还会改变数值结果。我们转而对生成的程序进行剖析，根据其自身语句及其读/写效果对其内存进行精确建模，并对这些语句进行重排。我们证明，只要内存分配不依赖于历史，该方法就能实现所建模的峰值。在我们所有的CPU运行中，它都能精确到字节地实现该峰值，且结果与原程序逐位一致。在GPU上，我们刻画了缓存分配器为何会破坏这一条件。为了知道何时应当停止，我们给出了前向……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出通过剖析并重排生成程序自身的语句来精确实现峰值内存调度，证明只要内存分配不依赖历史即可逐字节精确达到建模峰值且数值结果逐位一致，从而解决了将优化算子顺序交回编译器重新生成代码的不可靠问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes profiling and permuting the statements of generated programs to exactly realize peak-memory schedules, proving the modeled peak is achieved to the byte with bitwise-identical results whenever allocation is history-independent, thereby fixing the unreliability of handing optimized operator orders back to the compiler for code regeneration.
